idea.title: When your AI assistant should hand over to you
idea.angle: Smart human handoff: the moments a real agent must step in
idea.hook: The 7 moments your AI assistant should hand the chat to you

slides.heading: 7 moments your AI assistant should hand the chat **to you**
slides.body: A good system knows when to step back.

slides.heading: AI can answer fast. It **can't close** for you.
slides.body: A chatbot can reply at midnight and ask about budget. But some moments need a real agent. The system has to be built to spot them, not left to guess.

slides.heading: The buyer is **ready**
bullets: They ask to negotiate the price
They want to pay a deposit
They ask about documents or land title
They say 'can I talk to someone?'

slides.heading: Things get **sensitive**
bullets: The client sounds upset or confused
The question isn't in your listings or FAQs
It's a big buyer, like a diaspora client buying in Lekki

slides.heading: "Good question. Let me get Ama, our agent, to answer you directly. She'll message you shortly."
slides.body: Honest, warm, and it tells them a real person is coming.

slides.heading: "Hi, Ama here. I've read your chat, so no need to repeat yourself. About the deposit..."
slides.body: Pick up exactly where the AI stopped. Never make them start over.

slides.heading: It's the **system**, not the tool
slides.body: AI isn't smart on its own. Handoff rules, your listings and clear prompts make it work. That's how we build Kortexa: the AI does the fast part, you do the human part.

slides.heading: Save this before you set up **any chatbot**
slides.body: Follow @kortexa and DM 'SYSTEM' for a free trial

caption:
7 moments your AI assistant should hand the chat to you.

An AI assistant is great for fast replies and basic questions.
But negotiations, deposits and land title questions need you.
So do upset clients and anything outside your listings.
A good system spots these moments and passes the chat on cleanly.
A bad one keeps talking and loses the client.
